```text
# #4734: Patch: a finished game's board stops reading Enemy turn, and a board opened on a finished game shows its result at once
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Two things go wrong on the board once a game is over.

First, the End turn button reads "Enemy turn" after every game, even one the player has just won on their own turn. It sits right beside "Game over", and on a phone held upright it's the only turn wording left on screen. It will read "Game over".

Second, when a board opens on a game that is already over, the Victory or Defeat panel stays invisible and can't be clicked for nearly four seconds. It is waiting for a victory animation that never plays. One way to hit it: watch the replay straight after an online match, come back to the board to press Rematch, and nothing shows. After the fix it shows at once. A game that ends while the player is watching keeps its animation and the short wait before the panel.

## Why

- `apps/web/src/game/Board.tsx:632-633`: `ownTurn = view.result === null && view.active === view.viewer`, then `endTurnState = !ownTurn ? "enemy" : …`. Every finished view is therefore `enemy`, and `:822` labels it `t("Enemy turn")`. The turn plate beside it prints `t("Game over")` (`:802-803`). The only test of the label (`game/Board.test.tsx:90-103`) covers the opponent's live turn, not a finished game.
- `apps/web/src/game/Result.tsx:157-172`: the panel waits `resultRevealMs()` before it is revealed, and stays transparent and ignores the pointer until then. That is `FX_LETHAL_LEAD_MAX_MS` + `FX_RESULT_MS`, 600 + 3200 ms (`fx/constants.ts:13`, `:56`). The function's own comment says "with no effects to watch, 0".
- The effects layer plays the killing blow and Victory/Defeat only when a result arrives on a board that is already mounted. `apps/web/src/fx/FxLayer.tsx:446` starts `lastResult` at `undefined`, and `:464` plays only `if (previousResult === null && view.result !== null)`. A board mounted on a finished view has nothing to watch, yet waits the full 3.8 s.
- That mount happens in normal play. `apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx:440` replaces the board with the replay while it is watched, so Back from Watch the replay mounts a fresh board on the finished game. Rematch is hidden for those seconds. A page reloaded on a finished match does the same.
- Two tests pin the wait in exactly the case where nothing plays. `game/Game.test.tsx:324-333` ("waits out the effects layer's Victory / Defeat before it takes the pointer") mounts a finished view first. `routes/match.test.tsx:1162` pushes `finished` as its first view and expects `data-revealed="false"`.

## Proposal

1. **End turn after the game.** A view with a result gets its own End turn state, `over`. It is labelled `t("Game over")` (already in `zh-CN.json`), stays disabled as today, and is styled as the `enemy` state is (`game/board.css:2623` takes `over` beside `enemy`). The opponent's live turn still reads "Enemy turn".
2. **The result waits only for an animation that plays.** `Game` tells `GameResult` whether this result arrived on the mounted board: the shown view went from no result to a result, the condition `FxLayer` plays on. Only then does `GameResult` use `resultRevealMs()`; otherwise the wait is 0. Reduced motion and effects off stay 0, as today.
3. **One ruling note**, `spec/rulings/R<N>000.md`, records both, with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<N>.md`.

Rejected: hiding End turn once the game is over. It would shift the rail's layout at the moment the result comes in.

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/game/Board.tsx`, `apps/web/src/game/board.css`, `apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx`, `apps/web/src/game/Result.tsx`.
- Tests: `game/Board.test.tsx`, `game/Game.test.tsx`, `routes/match.test.tsx` (the two pinning tests push an unfinished view first, and new cases cover a finished mount).
- `spec/rulings/R<N>000.md` and `spec/pending/<N>.md`. §10.10 and R200 for the effects' timing, which stays as it is.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A finished view's End turn reads "Game over", carries `data-turn-state="over"` and is disabled. This holds for a win, a loss and a draw, whether the game ended on the viewer's turn or the opponent's.
- [ ] The opponent's live turn still reads "Enemy turn", and the existing assertion passes.
- [ ] A `Game` mounted on a finished view, effects on, shows its result panel with `data-revealed="true"` at once and no animation delay.
- [ ] A `Game` that receives its result while mounted still waits out the effects. The existing test is rewritten to mount an unfinished view and then rerender the finished one.
- [ ] In `routes/match`, after Watch the replay and Back, the result panel and its Rematch are revealed with no wait.
- [ ] Tests named `it("R<N>000 …")` sit in the note's `proven_in`, and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test` passes on the touched test files.

## Size and risks

Small: four source files, three test files and one ruling. Risk is low. A route that remounts its board at the moment the game ends now shows the panel at once, but nothing would have played there anyway. The e2e component specs that wait for `data-revealed="true"` (e.g. `e2e/cypress/component/rematch-buttons.cy.tsx:108`) reach it sooner and still pass.
```

# Plan for Issue #4734

## 1. Goal

On a finished game, the board's End turn button reads "Game over" instead of "Enemy turn", carries `data-turn-state="over"`, and remains disabled and styled as the enemy state was, for any outcome (win, loss, or draw) regardless of whose turn it ended on. When a board is mounted on an already finished game (e.g. returning to the board after watching a replay or reloading), the result panel and its rematch buttons are revealed immediately (`data-revealed="true"` with no 3.8s animation delay), while games ending while the board is mounted continue to wait out the effects layer's lethal and victory/defeat sequence. A new ruling note R4734000 records both presentation behaviors under SPEC §10.10 and R200.

## 2. Files to touch

## 3. Steps

       ```typescript
       const ownTurn = view.result === null && view.active === view.viewer;

         view.result !== null ? "over" : !ownTurn ? "enemy" : !endTurnLegal ? "locked" : actionsRemain ? "ready" : "waiting";
       ```

     ```markdown
     ---
     id: R4734000
     title: "A finished game's board stops reading Enemy turn, and a board opened on a finished game shows its result at once (issue #4734)"
     cards: "§10.10, R200, issue #4734"

     **Why.** Once a game was over, two presentation issues degraded the board's clarity (issue #4734):
     1. The End turn button read "Enemy turn" after every game, even a game the player won on their own turn. The turn plate beside it read "Game over", but on portrait viewports on mobile devices, End turn is the only turn wording visible.
     2. When a board mounted on a game already finished (for instance, returning to the match route after watching a replay, or reloading a page on a finished match), the Victory or Defeat panel stayed transparent and ignored pointers for 3.8 seconds (`resultRevealMs()`, 600 ms lethal lead + 3200 ms result sequence). The effects layer (`apps/web/src/fx/FxLayer.tsx`) only plays lethal and Victory/Defeat cues when a result arrives while mounted (`previousResult === null && view.result !== null`), so the panel was waiting out an animation that never played, preventing players from clicking Rematch immediately.

     **What holds now.**
     - When a game has a result (`view.result !== null`), End turn carries `data-turn-state="over"`, displays the label `t("Game over")`, and remains disabled (`disabled` and `aria-disabled="true"`). This holds regardless of whether the game was won, lost, or drawn, and whether it ended on the viewer's turn or the opponent's. The button shares the sunken, desaturated styling of the `enemy` state in `apps/web/src/game/board.css`.
     - The opponent's live turn (`view.result === null && view.active !== view.viewer`) continues to display "Enemy turn" with `data-turn-state="enemy"`.
     - `Game` tracks whether the board mounted on an in-progress game (`shown.result === null`). Only when the result arrived on the mounted board (transition from `result === null` to `result !== null`) does `GameResult` wait out `resultRevealMs()`; if the board mounted on an already-finished game, the reveal delay is 0, displaying the result panel with `data-revealed="true"` immediately. Reduced motion and disabled effects continue to reveal with 0 delay ([[R200]], [[§10.10]]).

     **Rejected.**
     - Hiding the End turn button once the game is over: this would shift the layout of the rail right when the result lands.
     - Retaining the 3.8-second delay when mounting on an already finished game: nothing plays in the effects layer on that mount, so the delay served only to block player input (such as Rematch).
     ```

     ```markdown
     **[[R4734000]] a finished game's board stops reading Enemy turn, and a board opened on a finished game shows its result at once (issue #4734, 2026-11-24)**: on a finished game, End turn carries `data-turn-state="over"`, reads "Game over" and stays disabled; the opponent's live turn still reads "Enemy turn". A board mounted on an already finished game shows its result panel at once (`data-revealed="true"` with no animation delay), since no killing blow or Victory/Defeat animation plays ([[R200]], [[§10.10]]); a board that receives its result while mounted still waits out the effects.
     ```

## 5. Done when

- [ ] `apps/web/src/game/board.css` styles `[data-turn-state="over"]` beside `[data-turn-state="enemy"]` at line 2623.
- [ ] `apps/web/src/game/Result.tsx` accepts `arrived?: boolean` and defaults reveal wait to 0 when false.
- [ ] `apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx` tracks `mountedLive = useRef(shown.result === null)` and passes `arrived={mountedLive.current}` to `GameResult`.
- [ ] `apps/web/src/game/Board.test.tsx` has `it("R4734000 ...")` passing, and opponent's live turn still asserts "Enemy turn".

## 6. Risks

- **Animation timing divergence between FxLayer and Result**: `FxLayer` plays the lethal lead and Victory/Defeat cues only on the condition `previousResult === null && view.result !== null`. If `GameResult` used a different condition or waited on initial mount, the panel would either appear over a running animation or stay invisible with nothing playing. By coupling `arrived` strictly to whether the board mounted on an in-progress game (`shown.result === null`), `GameResult` waits if and only if `FxLayer` triggers its cues.
- **Layout shift**: Hiding the End turn button upon game over was rejected because it would shift the rail layout right when the result arrives. Keeping the button visible in its `"over"` state with the same physical dimensions and sunken styling prevents layout jumping.
- **Rule 7 (Presentation purity)**: Neither End turn wording nor result reveal timing affects game state or sends illegal intents; legality remains governed by engine views.

None.
